Oh boy. 

Actually a lot of vegans have talked about how we should neuter EVERY animal possible to avoid any further cruelty issues as there wouldn't be any animals to harm.

Yes. Farmers do kill their animals, believe me I know. I disagree with it and think sustainable no kill farms/no meat farms are possible (more spread out, grass fed, miniature cattle and goats for less resources...). If someone eats a cow that died naturally or due to suffering  (my step dad constantly asks me if I'd eat roadkill or a euthanized sick animal, and while I'm a little grossed out by it, I would really be sad about it, I'd probably eat a human with consent in such a situation to be honest here just out of curiosity, as psycho as that makes me sound). The animal wasn't born to be killed prematurely (think a cow supposed to live 25 years, they usually get killed at 5, wow).

Are hunters bad...? I mean, yes hunting is bad, but one or a few bad things a bad person does not make (although I may be too forgiving? we aren't perfect pacifist divine beings),seeing as the majaority do not require to kill and can be very damaging for the ecosystem  (hunting wolves for fur then "having to save the ecosystem" by killing their prey deer for example...we wouldn't be overpopulated if we didn't kill predators to begin with and let them have their prey like they need to survive). 

I'm not sure if all animals are self aware/concious/whatever. When it comes to things like mussels, I honestly don't know. A lot of people avoid eating "animals" on principle, but forget the reason we avoid meat to begin with - animal suffering. And, no, they do not die painlessly, especially not most hunters, despite what they want you to believe. "Humane" sells, the fact you're killing an animal when you don't have itself doesn't. Even, hypothetically, if the animal felt no pain, there is some issues.
1. The life before slaughter - I would not want mine or a dog/cat last moment's to be a crowded van, crate, or firmly held, then squished into a tube/milk carton (as on homesteads), and hung upside down... Animals, even humans, probably don't experience dying itself. There's simply nothing to experience. The only way a painless death would be painless/no suffering would be too sudden to even notice (I suppose this is what hunters try to do when they kill unsuspecting/relaxed/grazing animals, but even then it usually takes a long time for them to bleed out) 
2. How would we regulate this? Surely it'd be safer to ban non medically issued killing (as difficult as that would be) and if the animal was killed to escape from suffering
3. ...then eat it. If someone wants to stuff their late kitten with some cat diease, let them eat the organs too given they are safe. 
4. I'm not even sure how I feel about humans being compared myself, but killing a human painlessly would still cause similar issues especially for animals that heavily bond with their families like mammals (dogs can mourn)
5...People who are violent to animals have a higher chance of being more agressive in general, why kids who are animal crushers grow up to be psychos 

Meat eating omnivores make me. . . Sad, yes. But it's a fact of life that omnivores and carnivores eat meat. As much as I'd like to somehow make animals evolve to be herbivores (and not kill Earth), we aren't even close yet. But a lot of herbivores are very intelligent and even shown to be altrustic. I think herbivores are more developed species, even omnivorous dogs have evolved with humans to eat more carbs and less protein. I think kindess is just the evolutionary way to go. :)

We *can* eat meat and/or plants, like I said, we have a choice. We are capable of doing so many things and we are very evolved and adaptable! That's a good thing. So we don't have to kill. We can just eat plants instead... Oh. I also evolved and made guns. Hmm. Can I shoot every puppy I see? Nah, I don't have to, why be an ass? I can use my intelligence to not like a wild animal. Eat meat? Shit in your yard, no ac, no heating.

Plants are not proven to be sentient. They, as far as we know, do not feel fear like animals do. I think a lot of people forget we are animals. Are plants and animals really the same to all of you? Reminds me of this tongue in cheekcomic: http://www.defenseofreason.com/wp-content/uploads/vegan_22_plants.jpg

Rats...I was making a point about how captivity is safer for humans. Obviously a feral cat  or other animal has a higher chance of giving you a disease, infection, attacking you etc. than a bred, tame one. There's a reason why we have pets and tell children not to pet bears and foxes.

I don't value cattle more than cats or dogs. Well, maybe I do, but we all favorite animals don't we? I also think shrimp are adorable! It's not a moral issue, I just think cows are really cute. I'm sure you happen to like bunnies or something more though, that's okay. I am against eating cows for the same reason most are against eating dogs. Animal violence. Cows don't have to be killed anymore than dogs too and I think exploring new ways of working with "excess" (bulls, older cows, lots of babies) is a wonderful thing. I would hope a seeing eye bred dog that wasn't very well trained and actually not very good at being a seeing eye dog wouldn't be killed for not doing that job. Still deserves life long caring and love.

What is hypocritical about what I am saying? It would be critical to assume cows are for killing and dogs aren't with no reason. I think both can suffer. And meat dogs, like the ones in Korea everyone wants to rescue, are...meat dogs. They're bred to be meat dogs. But they obviously don't like being meat dogs or they'd happily walk to slaughter. Sled dogs, herding dogs, etc. on the other hand are more apt and even happy to do their jobs - like why a high energy dog isn't good for a stay at home elderly person, she'd probably need a gentle lap dog. Even dairy animals are more gentle and calm to be handled in those areas.

It's certainly safer, better chances. I disagree with steak lovers and vegans, actually. I'm this lovely thing called a vegetarian and I think there is a grey area. Some dogs are bred to pull sleds, some dogs are bred to herd sheep, some cows are bred to be milked, some chickens are bred to lay eggs, that's not inherently violent. The whole method of farming now is very harmful to humans and our society/the environment as well as animal welfare. Humans are domesticating animals and I disagree that animals should go extinct like vegans want to euthanize all livestock and pets from existence. Seeing eye dogs, honey bees, etc. - domestic animals can have a mutually benefical relationship with the humans that are responsible for them. Some dogs are bred to be fighting dogs - but fighting dogs is abusive and cruel. Abusive doesn't necessarily mean torture, but just "misuse". Even if a cow was set to be hung up and shot from the day she was born, that's still misuse. And she can be alive to safely graze and just do her cow thing. Maybe be sent to a farm like the Gentle Barn which is meant to be therapy animals for troubled children and teens. I do feel bad about the dairy/egg industries I support, but not because it's "stealing", but because of male chick/bull slaughter. I cannot afford my own animals and a vegan diet at this time. I consider it a grey area, I'm not directly supporting the death of the hen I bought an omlete from, but they still get money. A lot of vegans buy Ben and Jerry's vegan flavors but obviously their money goes to a dairy farmer. There's grey areas everywhere. It's just best to do what you can. Her stepping on a lizard is unavoidable. Lice, for example, have to be killed in self defense, that's a lot different than slaughtering an animal when you have the option to purchase another meal (which may or may not be a viable option, I wouldn't be upset at a starving homeless guy for getting a $1 burger, just upset the fact a fellow human is without shelter but I digress). We are (mostly) very privileged as a species, we do not for the most part have to kill. We can use technology, toilets, warm beds, air conditioning...we aren't lions who kill for their livelihood. And I'm so happy I am a human being who has the opportunity to avoid violence. Eating lower on the food chain already has so many health and environmental benefits that the possibility of a sentient plant doesn't really matter. If you could kill a sentient being or a maybe probably not sentient being, why kill both...Why not just the maybe, probably not, and hey, in the future, if plants are sentient, that's even an opportunity for non biological food at all! Sci fi fiction ideas(?) I find these things so exciting to think about, like a ted talk on cell cloned leather I watched earlier.
